_meta.description: Anti-pattern library for CV and cover letter text: constructions that signal machine drafting, read as generic filler, or set the wrong tone. Scanned during composition, over every section including bullets.
_meta.usage: Each anti-pattern has a pattern to look for, a description of why it hurts, and a bad and fixed example. The scan flags every match in the composed text with its id. The user decides whether to revise. Category 'claude-ism' means a pattern typical of AI assistant drafting, whichever assistant produced it.

anti_patterns.pattern: isn't X, it's Y / not X -- Y / not X; it's Y
anti_patterns.description: False contrast that performs insight rather than delivering it. Creates a dramatic reveal where a plain statement would land harder.
anti_patterns.example_bad: This isn't a side project. It's a working product.
anti_patterns.example_fix: The scheduling app has run for a local club since spring.

anti_patterns.pattern: not just X, but Y / not only X, but also Y
anti_patterns.description: False modesty escalator. Pretends to understate, then stacks. Reads as formulaic.
anti_patterns.example_bad: Not just an analyst, but a trusted advisor to the business.
anti_patterns.example_fix: Department heads asked me to review their process changes before sign-off.

anti_patterns.pattern: truly / deeply / exceptionally / incredibly / remarkably + adjective
anti_patterns.description: Adverb inflation. Intensifiers stand in for a fact that should speak for itself.
anti_patterns.example_bad: I am an incredibly thorough and deeply organised planner.
anti_patterns.example_fix: I planned the office move; the team lost no working days.

anti_patterns.pattern: I should be honest / to be candid / if I'm being transparent / I'll be direct
anti_patterns.description: Announcing honesty instead of being honest. The preface undermines the candour it claims.
anti_patterns.example_bad: To be candid, I have not used this reporting tool before.
anti_patterns.example_fix: I have not used this reporting tool; I have built similar reports in two others.

anti_patterns.pattern: Furthermore / Additionally / Moreover / In addition / What's more
anti_patterns.description: Academic transition words. They add no meaning, consume word count, and signal template writing.
anti_patterns.example_bad: Moreover, I have worked with several reporting tools.
anti_patterns.example_fix: I rebuilt the monthly sales report in a new reporting tool; it now runs itself.

anti_patterns.pattern: I believe / I feel that / I think I can / I would say
anti_patterns.description: Hedging weakens claims. In a CV or cover letter, either the user did it or did not.
anti_patterns.example_bad: I feel that my organisational strengths would suit your team.
anti_patterns.example_fix: I set up the team rota that cut overtime by a fifth.

anti_patterns.pattern: passionate about / passion for / driven by a passion
anti_patterns.description: Empty enthusiasm. Everyone claims passion. Evidence of sustained effort says it without the word.
anti_patterns.example_bad: I am passionate about data and its power to transform organisations.
anti_patterns.example_fix: I have run a weekly data clinic for colleagues for the past year.

anti_patterns.description: Corporate buzzwords. They mean nothing specific. Replace with what actually happened.
anti_patterns.example_bad: Leveraged digital tools to create holistic customer solutions.
anti_patterns.example_fix: Replaced the paper order form with an online one; orders arrived complete.

anti_patterns.pattern: dynamic / team player / results-driven / detail-oriented / self-starter
anti_patterns.description: CV filler words. Universally claimed, never differentiating. Show the quality through evidence instead.
anti_patterns.example_bad: A dynamic self-starter with a results-driven mindset.
anti_patterns.example_fix: I checked every supplier record before the migration and fixed 40 that would have failed.

anti_patterns.pattern: ! in professional text / I'm excited to / thrilled to
anti_patterns.description: Forced enthusiasm. Calm confidence reads stronger than performed excitement in written applications.
anti_patterns.example_bad: I am so excited to apply for this position!
anti_patterns.example_fix: Your team is moving its customer records to a new platform; I led the same move at my last employer.

anti_patterns.description: Flattery disguised as enthusiasm. Comes across as desperate rather than considered.
anti_patterns.example_bad: This is my dream role and a once-in-a-lifetime chance.
anti_patterns.example_fix: The role combines process design and reporting, the two things I have done most in the last three years.

anti_patterns.pattern: two or more em dashes (or raw double hyphens) in one paragraph
anti_patterns.description: Assistants over-use dashes for parenthetical asides. Maximum one per paragraph. Two or more signal machine drafting. Replace the extras with commas, colons or full stops.
anti_patterns.example_bad: The new form -- launched in a month -- cut errors -- and staff liked it.
anti_patterns.example_fix: The new form launched in a month and cut errors. Staff liked it.

anti_patterns.pattern: X, Y, and Z endings repeated across consecutive sentences or bullets
anti_patterns.description: Assistants default to three-item lists. Natural writing varies sentence structure. Two consecutive tricolons is a flag.
anti_patterns.example_bad: I listen, question, and clarify. I plan, test, and deliver.
anti_patterns.example_fix: I ask questions until the problem is clear. Then I test a fix with the people who reported it.

anti_patterns.pattern: nobody else / I found it because I looked / that's how I work / not because anyone assigned it / nobody had bothered
anti_patterns.description: Frames initiative as isolation. Implies the team was asleep and the applicant is the only competent person. Many hiring cultures penalise this: confidence should be understated, results should speak, and collegiality matters. Frame initiative as a contribution to the team, not a contrast against it.
anti_patterns.example_bad: I was the only one who spotted the billing errors.
anti_patterns.example_fix: I raised the billing errors at the weekly review, and the team fixed them before month end.

anti_patterns.pattern: which channels, tools or ticket mechanics a thing sat in: chat threads, shared inboxes, email chains, ticket counts, 'scattered across informal channels'
anti_patterns.description: Operational detail about tooling instead of the outcome for the business. In a cover letter the reader asks why it matters. Letters carry outcomes: what changed for the people using the work, what got simpler, what fell. Channel and tool detail belongs, at most, in a working log, not in a letter or a lead bullet.
anti_patterns.example_bad: I found that half of all requests were sitting in chat threads and shared inboxes.
anti_patterns.example_fix: Requests had no single route in. I gave them one; response times fell by a third.
